findings.summary: CHECK for FR-015 is a gate that cannot fail over 58% of the driver: its OCaml-comment stripper treats `(*` inside a SQL string literal as a comment opener, so `count(*)` opens a phantom comment that never closes and 1288 of 2215 lines are stripped before scanning.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-no-score.sh:57 — `if (depth == 0 && two == "(*") { depth = 1 }`; opened by bin/arch_mutants/arch_mutants.ml:1024 `count(*) FROM mutant_kills`. Positive control executed: injecting a printf with the word `score` and a literal `%%` on an output path at :1685 produced exit 0 and 'PASS — 0 offending site(s)'. Measured end-of-file depth 3; 1288 of 2215 lines never scanned.
findings.fix: Strip string literals before scanning for comment delimiters, as check-status-provenance.sh:56 already does. Re-run the same positive control and require exit 1. Count lines actually scanned at depth 0, not physical lines.
findings.check_note: Recorded as a spec-level CHECK id, not a node-runnable path: the file is checks/no-score-scans-sql-strings.sh, a bash script. It exits 0 under bash at 9e22f64 and was independently red-verified this round by restoring its own target from 42e6ee5. The convergence gate invokes checks as `node <path>`, where a shell script fails on its first line — which is why this is recorded for traceability rather than gate-executed.

findings.summary: CHECK-7 does not check the enclosing record, contrary to its own header. A nested `Assoc never opens its own record, so an inner record inherits any selection_provenance key appearing anywhere in the outer one.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-status-provenance.sh:80 — `if (depth == 0 && raw ~ /`Assoc/)`. Positive control executed: deleting only the per-run record's provenance key at arch_mutants.ml:1584, leaving that record emitting engine_status with no provenance beside it, produced exit 0 and 'PASS — 0 offending emitter(s)'. That per-mutant row is the one a reader copies into a bug report — the case FR-013 exists for.
findings.fix: Maintain a stack: open a record at every `Assoc, not only at depth 0, and judge each record against the keys inside its own brackets. Re-run the same deletion and require exit 1.

findings.summary: When the wrapper wrote no trace line, the driver silently substitutes the PLANNED set and records it as executed — then writes a mutant_kills row with attribution singleton_executed_set naming a test never observed running.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1425-1427 — `let executed = Option.value ~default:sel.sel_executed (Hashtbl.find_opt executed_by_id sel.sel_site.s_id)`; consumed at :1443-1446 `MDb.insert_kill ~attribution:MDb.Singleton_executed_set`. Same fallback at :1575 and :1703. Nothing reconciles the trace against attempted.
findings.fix: Make the lookup total: a mutant with no trace line has an UNOBSERVED executed set. It must receive no kill row under any attribution, the count must appear in both formats, and completed_at must not be stamped while any attempted mutant lacks a trace line.

findings.summary: The wrapper's refusal is indistinguishable from a kill at the engine boundary: fail() exits 2 and the engine reads 'anything else = killed'. A wholly broken selection produces a campaign of clean kills instead of a refusal.
findings.evidence: scripts/mutaml-wrapper.sh:41 — `fail() { ...; exit 2; }` against its own :32-33 'the test command's own exit code, which is what the engine reads (0 = SURVIVED, 124 = timeout, anything else = killed)'. fail() exits before :85 so no trace line is written, which then triggers the fallback at arch_mutants.ml:1426.
findings.fix: Route the refusal through a channel the engine cannot recolour: append a refusal line to $ARCH_MUTANTS_TRACE before exiting, and have the driver treat any mutant with a refusal line as not-attempted — never KILLED, never eligible for attribution, and enough to keep completed_at NULL.

findings.summary: A mutant the index could map to no function publishes SURVIVED under proved_superset — a positive claim that every reaching test ran, for a mutant whose reaching set was never computed.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1263 — `let intended = match !best with Some tg -> tg.t_tests | None -> []`, with sel_fn = None at :1266; the wrapper then runs nothing and the engine reports SURVIVED. provenance is one campaign-wide value (:1201-1205) stored at :1433, so published_verdict (arch_mutant_db.ml:136-140) yields V_survived. The text surface says '(unmapped)' but the verdict, the counts and the JSON do not.
findings.fix: Provenance must be per-mutant in at least this respect: a mutant with sel_fn = None has no proved cone and must never carry proved_superset. Add a tezt case asserting the verdict of an unmapped survivor on a closed sound cone — none of the 20 cases covers it.

findings.summary: Shell injection through the {tests} substitution: test names are interpolated unquoted into a string handed to sh -c. Test names originate in the analysed repository's own source, so running a campaign over an untrusted checkout is arbitrary command execution.
findings.evidence: scripts/mutaml-wrapper.sh:73-75 — `cmd="${ARCH_MUTANTS_TEST_CMD//\{tests\}/${tests[*]}}"` then `sh -c "$cmd"`. Executed proof: a selection line whose executed field was `a;touch .../PWNED;echo x` with ARCH_MUTANTS_TEST_CMD='echo RUNNING {tests}' exited 0 and created PWNED. The sibling branch at :79 is safe — it passes the array through "$@".
findings.fix: Quote each element before substituting (printf '%q ' over the array) or drop the {tests} form and always use the "$@" path. The driver should additionally reject a test name containing shell metacharacters when writing selection.tsv.

findings.summary: `report` buckets any unrecognised engine status as ERRORED instead of refusing, so a misspelled or newly-added status is counted as an error rather than a survivor — a defect removed from the defect list with no crash and no log.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:395-397 — `if st = "KILLED" || st = "TIMEOUT" then incr killed else if st <> "SURVIVED" then incr errored`. The value comes from load_generic:307 which reads status as a bare string with no vocabulary check, unlike load_mutaml (:344-350) and MDb.status_of_string (:71-77). Reachable through `report --from generic`, which --fail-on-survivors gates CI on.
findings.fix: Route the generic path through MDb.status_of_string and die on None, then match totally on the variant. That removes the last if-chain over the closed vocabulary.

findings.summary: CHECK-17's stated exclusion is shaped exactly around the one violation left in the tree: it documents that a member inside an `if x = "KILLED"` test is not counted, and the surviving dispatch is written in precisely that form.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-total-matches.sh:23 — '# a member appearing on the RIGHT of ->, or inside an `if x = "KILLED"` test, is not an arm and is not counted'. The uncounted site is arch_mutants.ml:396-397. Positive control executed: a real `| _ -> incr errored` arm injected at :1424 IS caught (exit 1), so the script works for match arms — the shape it cannot see is the shape the code uses.
findings.fix: Extend the script to flag an if/else-if chain over two or more vocabulary members whose final else produces a value, or fix arch_mutants.ml:395-397 to match on the variant. The second is preferable: it removes the shape rather than teaching the lint about it.

findings.summary: mutants.function_id is never populated — the sole write site passes ~function_id:None unconditionally, making the column, its index and the EC-4 staleness story inert.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1338 — `~function_id:None ~function_name:sel.sel_fn`, the only call to MDb.insert_mutant. Against mutants-schema-migration.sql:76 (REFERENCES functions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL), :83 (the EC-4 paragraph) and :90 (idx_mutants_fnid). check-mutant-key.sh's 'rows with NULL function' line will report 100% for every campaign — a fact about this code path, not the population.
findings.fix: Resolve the plan target's function id and pass it, or drop the column, its index and the EC-4 paragraph so the schema stops documenting behaviour no run can produce.

findings.summary: Assessed, not restated: the exit-3 design is right, but every LAYER built on the unobserved premise is also unobserved — that the engine reads the wrapper's exit code as the verdict, that a refusal is recoloured as a kill, that a trace line reaches the driver. Three HIGH findings live in exactly that band.
findings.evidence: scripts/check-mutaml-integration.sh executed -> exit 3, 'UNVERIFIED — no mutaml-runner on PATH'. specs/mutation-campaign-313.md:275 AC-20 is satisfiable by 'the report states it is unverified', so this is not a spec violation; it is a statement that the mechanism has zero runtime evidence.
findings.fix: Install mutaml or point MUTAML_RUNNER at a built runner.exe and run this before merge; it is the only thing that can settle the exit-code-recolouring question. If it cannot be run, name the three unobserved behaviours explicitly in the PR body.

findings.summary: AC-20 is unverified: CHECK-8 exits 3 because no mutaml is installed, so the campaign's core mechanism has never been observed running.
findings.evidence: Observed: exit 3, 'UNVERIFIED — no mutaml-runner on PATH and MUTAML_RUNNER is unset. Do not read this as a pass.' This is what AC-20 (spec:243) prescribes for the absent-engine case. Recorded so the coverage table is not read as green.
findings.fix: No code change. Ensure the PR body carries the exit-3 line verbatim so a merge reviewer cannot read CHECK-8 as covered.

findings.summary: executed_superset is decided by comparing LENGTHS, not by testing set inclusion, yet it is stored and published as the claim that the executed set contains the intended one.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1269 — `sel_superset = List.length executed > List.length sel.sel_intended`, repeated at :1436 and :1587-1588. Under Group the expansion falls back to [name], so an intended name can be absent while the counts coincide. Under Suite and Case inclusion holds by accident of the other two arms.
findings.fix: Compute inclusion over a set and refuse (or record no-observation) when the intended set is not contained — a non-superset executed set is under-selection, the failure the module's own docstring at :506-508 says must never happen.

findings.summary: --max-list silently defaults to 20 on an unparseable value — the one place in this CLI that guesses rather than refuses.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2085 — `match int_of_string_opt (opt "--max-list" "20") with Some n -> n | None -> 20`. Contrast --campaign (:2180), --profile (:2143) and --from (:2131), which all die with an explicit 'not defaulted' rationale.
findings.fix: Die naming the bad value, matching --campaign two dozen lines below.

findings.summary: The only unparameterised SQL interpolation in the change. Not exploitable today because only_campaign is an int, but it is safe only because of a validation two hundred lines away in a different function.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1894 — `(match only_campaign with Some n -> Printf.sprintf "WHERE id = %d" n | None -> "")`. Every other query in the change binds its values (arch_mutant_db.ml:244-299, and findings_of_runs at :1820-1824).
findings.fix: Use the parameterised form already available: two SELECT texts and ~params_ty:Arch_db.Ty.int binding the id.

findings.summary: Assessed, not restated: the four flags beyond the sub-brief's grammar are the right call and the right shape; three of the four refuse rather than default. The one that defaults (--report) is benign because a missing report yields an empty outcomes list, every mutant becomes PENDING and complete stays false.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2152-2160 the --catalogue refusal; :2162-2166 the --report default; :1377-1379 the empty-outcomes path.
findings.fix: No change. Name the --report default in the run output alongside engine_path and test_runner_path, so a campaign that read no report says which path it looked at.

findings.summary: FR-001 states run MUST accept `<db> --plan <file> --engine <cmd>`; the implementation refuses that exact invocation because --catalogue is mandatory.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2152-2159 dies without --catalogue. FR-001 (spec:154) and C-2's fixed grammar (:135) list only --plan, --engine and three optional flags. The deviation is disclosed in the impl brief and defensible on the merits, but the spec is status: live and still declares the narrower grammar.
findings.fix: Amend FR-001 and C-2 to the four-flag grammar with the refusal semantics, so the live spec and the binary agree.

findings.summary: Assessed, not restated: 'group' as the test's source file is defensible for slice 1 and only ever widens, but neither output format says what a group was taken to mean — and slice 5 is expected to harden it, so a campaign persisted under the current meaning will not be distinguishable from one under the next.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1238-1244 — the Group arm of expand, keyed on test_file then tests_in_file.
findings.fix: Emit the definition next to the granularity in both formats, so a stored campaign carries the meaning its numbers were computed under.

findings.summary: Engine outcomes are joined to catalogued mutant sites by (basename, line) only, discarding the columns and replacement text the mutants UNIQUE key is built from — so two mutants on one line get their statuses paired arbitrarily.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1393 `when sel.sel_site.s_line = m.line` / :1394 `&& base sel.sel_site.s_file = base m.file ->`, while mutants-schema-migration.sql:88 declares UNIQUE(file_path, line, col_start, col_end, replacement, source_hash) and :1433 stores ~engine_mutant_id from the CATALOGUE's id, never the report entry's — so a mispairing leaves no trace in the traceability column either.
findings.fix: Join on the engine's own id (the report record already carries it at :293); fall back to (file, line, replacement); when two catalogued sites on one line remain indistinguishable, refuse rather than consuming duplicates in list order.
findings.reopen_note: Re-found by the round-3 review on this HEAD, by two specialists independently.
findings.replay_note: Replayed BY CONTENT at 4e4ca5b by the reviewer, not accepted from the implementing agent's report. the basename join survives ONLY as a history comment at :2443 ('The join was first [Filename.basename ...'). same_path is full-path equality; by_site discriminates on cols, replacement and the occurrence ordinal; refuse_ambiguous exists at two sites. Every named ratchet was itself re-proved by the reviewer: red against the pre-fix tree via git checkout <sha> -- <path> then rebuild, green after, no git stash.
findings.closure_species_method: computed by the same classifier on both sides (2026-09-06 correction)

findings.summary: A --diff scope that narrows the catalogue to zero mutants produces a COMPLETED campaign with zero run rows, which verdict publishes as all-zero counts — the exact 'empty reads as no survivors' conflation the rest of the design refuses.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1456 `let complete = (not refused) && engine_code = 0 && pending = 0`, where catalogued is the POST-narrowing list (:1454, after the List.partition at :1287). load_catalogue's empty-catalogue refusal (:683) fires before narrowing and cannot see this. verdict_cmd prints only the per-verdict counts (:2020) with no zero-findings guard.
findings.fix: Refuse in run_campaign when --diff narrows selections to empty, with load_catalogue:683's wording; and have verdict_cmd state 'this campaign attempted nothing' when a completed campaign yields zero findings.

findings.summary: The process boundary to arch-impact refuses only a MISSING touched key; a present-but-empty array, or entries whose name field is renamed, silently yields an empty touched set — the outcome the refusal message says it exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:938 `| None -> None)` inside the List.filter_map, versus the die at :941 claiming it refuses 'an empty set, which would select nothing and read as nothing to test'. That die is reachable only from the `| _ ->` arm at :940; `Some (`List [])` reaches Impact_ok at :929 with an empty list, and so does a list of objects with a renamed name field.
findings.fix: Refuse on Impact_ok [] at the call site (compute_diff_scope:1075) with the same message, and count entries dropped for a missing name and refuse if that count is non-zero — a silently shrunk touched set is indistinguishable from a correct small one.

findings.summary: producer_run_id is hardcoded to None by the only writer, so the documented link from a campaign to the index run it was driven against is never populated — and campaign rows survive a re-index, leaving stale verdicts indistinguishable from current ones.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1324 `MDb.insert_campaign db ~engine ~engine_version ~seed ~producer_run_id:None`, against mutants-schema-migration.sql:37. The four mutant tables are absent from lib/arch_index/arch_index_support.ml:56 schema_tables_to_drop, so a re-index of different code leaves every campaign row readable as current.
findings.fix: Read the current producer_runs id at campaign-insert time when the table exists. NULL must mean 'this index has no producer_runs table', not 'the writer never asked'.

findings.summary: Schema version 1.13 is stamped by the main-schema indexer, but architecture-schema.sql creates none of the four mutant tables — so a 1.13 database may carry zero of them and an unmigrated 1.11 database that arch-mutants wrote carries all four. The version does not gate the fact it claims to.
findings.evidence: lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml:71 `let current_schema_version = "1.13"`, stamped unconditionally at arch_index.ml:430-431; `grep -c mutant architecture-schema.sql` returns 0; the tables are created instead by arch_mutant_db.ml's open_and_migrate, and every consumer gates on Arch_db.has_table, never on the version.
findings.fix: Either fold the four tables into architecture-schema.sql so the stamp is truthful, or record a separate version key for the campaign schema (the precedent current_flat_schema_version exists at arch_index_db.ml:98) and narrow the docs/schema.md claim.

findings.summary: The burned-1.12 protocol is sound as arithmetic but has no mechanical reservation: nothing in code or tests prevents a third session deducing 1.12 again, which is the very failure the row was written to stop.
findings.evidence: docs/schema.md:275 records the burn in prose; the only other trace is the comment at lib/arch_index/arch_index_db.ml:63-70. A repo-wide grep of tezt/ and scripts/ for a burned-number or schema.md-sync check returns nothing.
findings.fix: Add a check (a tezt case or a scripts/check-*.sh, matching the seven this branch ships) parsing docs/schema.md's version column: strictly increasing, last row equals current_schema_version, fail on reuse of a burned row. That turns an assigned number into an enforced one.

findings.summary: The report subcommand publishes survivors — and gates CI via --fail-on-survivors — with no selection provenance at all, so FR-013, the rule this branch introduces, is bypassed by an entire command surface.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:475 prints '%d test(s) reach it and none killed it' with no provenance term anywhere in report (no hit for provenance between :417 and :1198), while :1465 states 'FR-013: never a status without its provenance, in either format' and :2189 lets --fail-on-survivors exit 1 on that same unqualified list.
findings.fix: Compute cone_escapes/contract_ok in report as run does at :1199-1204 and print the caveat next to every survivor; make --fail-on-survivors fail only on survivors whose derived verdict is V_survived.

findings.summary: prior_mutants reads engine_status out of the database WITHOUT selection_provenance and collapses it to a boolean, so a SURVIVED recorded under a ⊤-bounded selection is treated as a proven non-kill when scoping the --diff re-check set.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1022 — the projection has no r.selection_provenance; :1016 sets pk_killed from the status alone and :1146 uses it to decide the un-recheckable list. This is the caller the type design at arch_mutant_db.ml:117 was built to make impossible — the pairing is enforced in verdict (:1811) but not here.
findings.fix: Select r.selection_provenance alongside the status, build an MDb.outcome and branch on MDb.published_verdict rather than on a boolean. Better: make the SQL projection the only place a status is read, returning outcome by construction.

findings.summary: The reaching-test lower bound is still written twice — cone_escapes was extracted for the escapes half but the backward-closure fold remains duplicated verbatim between plan and report.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:417 is character-for-character the fold at :133, including the identical elements/filter_map/sort tail. The extraction rationale at :87 applies unchanged to this pair.
findings.fix: Extract reaching_tests next to cone_escapes and call it from both sites. The duplication predates this branch, but the branch extracts its sibling and the campaign's stated purpose is noticing duplicate call sites.

findings.summary: opt takes the FIRST occurrence of a flag and silently ignores later ones, so a duplicated --catalogue drives a campaign from one file while the operator believes it used the other.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2057 `let rec go = function a :: v :: _ when a = name -> v | _ :: tl -> go tl | [] -> default`. The same function serves --catalogue (:2153), --plan, --report, --diff and --engine; a trailing flag with no value also falls through to the default.
findings.fix: Collect all occurrences and die on more than one, and die on a value-taking flag with no value — the file already refuses every other ambiguous input on exactly this reasoning.

findings.summary: A missing report file yields zero outcomes and exit 0, so a CI job that mis-defaults --report gets a green run for a campaign that attempted nothing.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1377 `if Sys.file_exists report_path then ... else []`, with the exit computed at :1715 as `finish (if refused then 3 else 0)`. The campaign is correctly left open and the report says Nothing_attempted, but the exit code does not.
findings.fix: Exit non-zero (2, as every other unresolvable input does) when the report path does not exist, or when the certification tag is Nothing_attempted. A tag a consumer must read prose to find is not a gate.

findings.summary: One --from flag governs the format of two independently-supplied files, so a mutaml catalogue with a generic report is not expressible and the mismatch is discovered only as unmatched entries.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:2131 `let from = opt "--from" "generic"`, consumed at :1208 for the catalogue and :1378 for the report. A report covering every catalogued line still sets complete (:1456) even when !unmatched > 0.
findings.fix: Split into --catalogue-format and --report-format, and refuse to stamp completed_at when !unmatched > 0 — entries no catalogued site claims are evidence the two files came from different invocations.

findings.summary: The verdict surface structurally cannot scope PENDING once a database holds a second campaign, and closing it is named in-code as another schema change — so the first roadmap item that runs two campaigns against one index makes verdict refuse.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1951 the REFUSED (exit 3) message, with the remedy stated at :1942: a campaign_id on a catalogue table or a mutant_campaign_sites join, 'a schema change and therefore a version bump, which this slice does not own'.
findings.fix: None required now — the refusal is the honest surface. Record it as a scheduled 1.14 item; the additive table is cheap, but the CLI contract (exit 3 on a common case) is the part expensive to undo once consumers depend on it.

findings.summary: FR-030/AC-24 has no implementation anywhere in the driver: both binary resolvers walk ancestor directories with no tree-boundary check — exactly issue #77's mechanism — and CHECK-15 never exercises either of them.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:880-887 walks parents for _build/default/bin/arch_impact/arch_impact.exe with no comparison against the tree root; identically at :791-799 for locate_wrapper. FR-030 (spec:266-270) demands refusal when a resolved binary lies outside the working tree, AC-24 demands exit 1. The only guard is a die when an env override names a non-existent path (:790, :878), a different requirement. scripts/check-binary-provenance.sh:27-30 probes four hardcoded _build paths from the tree root and never calls arch-mutants, so it exits 0 on a tree where this feature was never written.
findings.fix: Add refuse_outside_tree ~root applied to locate_wrapper, locate_impact, engine_path and runner_path (:1166-1195), exiting 1 per AC-24; add a tezt case nesting a tree inside a parent checkout with an incomplete _build and assert exit 1. If the narrowing to the wrapper stands, amend FR-030 rather than leaving AC-24 unimplemented.

findings.summary: FR-031 forbids a catch-all over a CHECK-declared vocabulary, but report consumes the engine-status set through an if-chain whose negative arm is a catch-all; the status is never validated and CHECK-17 is structurally blind to the shape.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:396-397. The value comes from load_generic:307 which accepts any JSON string, unlike load_mutaml (:340-350) and run (:1411-1418). A member added to mutant_runs.engine_status's CHECK (migration:110-111) is counted as errored with no crash and no log — FR-031's stated failure mode verbatim. check-total-matches.sh:69-72 only inspects lines matching an arm pattern, so an if-chain is invisible: PASS, 0 offending arms over 290, exit 0.
findings.fix: Give load_generic load_mutaml's four-value refusal, then replace :396-397 with a total match. Extend check-total-matches.sh to flag if-chains over the same member lists, or state in its header that if-chains are out of its reach.

findings.summary: FR-002 requires the intended and executed test SETS to be recorded; the schema records only their cardinalities, and AC-2's 'intended set preserved' is asserted against a temporary file that does not survive the campaign.
findings.evidence: migration:127-129 stores intended_tests/executed_tests as INTEGER; arch_mutants.ml:1433-1436 passes List.length of each. The sets go only to selection.tsv under $TMPDIR (:1291-1309) and to stdout JSON (:1585-1588). tezt/tests/mutants.ml:568-571 asserts the executed set against that temp file while the DB assertion (:576-582) checks counts only. US-2's stated purpose is 'so that a later campaign can answer questions about an earlier one', which counts cannot.
findings.fix: Either add a mutant_run_tests(run_id, test_name, role) table (a schema bump) so the sets persist, or amend FR-002/AC-2 to say cardinalities-plus-transient-file is what 'record' means and state where the sets live.

findings.summary: CHECK-14 is declared for AC-21 and AC-22, but its test asserts nothing about the resolved binary paths; AC-22 has no assertion anywhere in the suite.
findings.evidence: spec:308 declares CHECK-14 covering AC-21 and AC-22. The registered test at tezt/tests/mutants.ml:688 asserts the certification tag and the killed/survived/errored counts only (:717-744). grep for engine_path/test_runner_path in the suite returns only column lists inside hand-written INSERT fixtures (:1003, :1307, :1472, :1480, :1488), never an assertion. FR-028 is implemented (arch_mutants.ml:1325, :1546-1548) but unverified.
findings.fix: Assert the JSON carries engine_path and test_runner_path equal to the fixture's resolved stub paths, and that the stored campaign row matches.

findings.summary: THE REPAIRED GUARD REINTRODUCED ITS OWN VACUITY IN A NEW FORM. The replacement scanner has no end-of-file guard for an unterminated string or unclosed comment, so a single OCaml char literal '"' anywhere in bin/arch_mutants makes it scan ZERO records and still print PASS. Its sibling check-no-score.sh emits both diagnostics, so the omission is inconsistent inside the same fix.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED positive control. Fixture A with `(* a doc comment holding a char literal: '"' *)` before an `Assoc carrying engine_status without provenance -> 'inspected 0 JSON record(s)', 'PASS — 0 offending emitter(s)', exit 0. Fixture B byte-identical minus the char literal -> exit 1. The END block at :157-166 tests only top > 0; cdepth and instr are never checked, unlike check-no-score.sh:111-114.
findings.fix: Emit a hit when cdepth != 0 and when instr, exactly as check-no-score.sh does, and treat a char literal as a single token before the quote arm.

findings.summary: A survivor that cannot be mapped to an indexed function still publishes a bare SURVIVED with no verdict and no provenance, under top_bounded. The round-2 fix removed that shape from the survivors array and left it in the unmapped array; the text rendering gives unmapped survivors no verdict at all. The ratchet check cannot see it, and check-status-provenance.sh exempts report's status key on a rationale the fix itself made false.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED: index with a ⊤ edge inside the test cone, report record for lib/zzz_unmapped.ml:999. report --format json exit 0 emitted survivors_publish_as UNKNOWN at document level while the unmapped element was {file,line,status:SURVIVED,id,mutation} — no verdict, no selection_provenance. Text mode printed only the location. Source arch_mutants.ml:588.
findings.fix: Give unmapped records the same three keys mapped survivors get and print the verdict in text; delete the now-false exclusion at check-status-provenance.sh:24-27 and extend the ratchet to cover an unmapped survivor.

findings.summary: guard_inside_tree does not fire when the inner checkout is not itself a git repository: git rev-parse then returns the ENCLOSING repo's root, the boundary spans both trees, and the outer tree's wrapper is handed to the engine. That is issue #77 exactly, unrefused. git init alone flips the guard.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED pair on one fixture. Inner NOT a repo -> engine stub printed 'ENGINE GOT WRAPPER: .../outer/scripts/mutaml-wrapper.sh', campaign written, exit 0, no refusal. After git init -q in the inner tree, byte-identical invocation -> exit 1 naming the outside path. checks/tree-boundary-refusal.sh's make_inner always runs git init, so it cannot see case (a).
findings.fix: Anchor on the nearer of the git toplevel and a tree-local marker of the campaign's own checkout, and add a probe whose inner tree is NOT git-initialised, red-verified.
findings.reopen_note: Re-found by the round-3 review on this HEAD, by two specialists independently.
findings.replay_note: Replayed BY EXECUTION at d98277e by group R4-B, not by reading: checks/tree-boundary-non-git-checkout.js probe 1 -- inner checkout NOT git-initialised, nested inside an outer repo, outer wrapper reached by the ancestor walk -- exits 1 and names the outside path. The described failure mode (engine handed the outer wrapper, campaign written, exit 0) does not occur. Closed against CHECK-40, which was red-verified when it was written and is green here. What would have made this non-zero: probe 1 accepting the outer wrapper.

findings.summary: The shell-injection allowlist excludes the apostrophe, an ordinary OCaml identifier character (aux', loop', test_foo'). One such name anywhere in the reaching set aborts the ENTIRE campaign at exit 2 with no campaign row — though the wrapper already POSIX-quotes each name, so the apostrophe is the one excluded character the quoting demonstrably handles.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED: index with a test function named test_alpha' reaching lib/x.ml:15 -> run exit 2, 'the test name "test_alpha'", reaching mutant 1 at lib/x.ml:15, carries a character outside the allowed set. No campaign row was written.' The refusal is clearly worded; only its reachability is at issue.
findings.fix: Allow the apostrophe at arch_mutants.ml:1616-1619 and keep refusing comma, tab and newline — the separators the refusal message itself argues for. Add a tezt case with a prime-suffixed name running to completion.

findings.summary: report's headline count excludes unmapped survivors from every bucket, so a report containing one SURVIVED mutant prints '1 mutant(s) in the report: 0 survived, 0 killed'. findings.evidence: EXECUTED, same fixture: '1 mutant(s) in the report: 0 survived, 0 killed' followed by '1 survivor(s) could not be mapped to an indexed function'. arch_mutants.ml:599 uses List.length survivors, which excludes unmapped.

findings.summary: CHECK-8's UNVERIFIED is a ONE-FLAG FIX, not a fixture limitation. mutaml-runner 0.3 resolves --muts relative to --build-context, which defaults to _build/default. Adding --build-context . makes the check pass against the real installed runner, turning the branch's one unverified integration into a verified one.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED. Unpatched with MUTAML_RUNNER set: exit 2, 'Could not read file lib/x.muts - _build/default/lib/x.muts'. With --build-context . added at :100: exit 0 — 'runner exited 0 · wrapper invocations : 2 · lib/x:1 resolved to : t_alpha · lib/x:2 resolved to : t_beta,t_gamma'. Bare invocation still exits 3 as expected.
findings.fix: Pass --build-context . at :100 and note in the header that the runner resolves --muts under the build context, so a future reader does not re-diagnose it as a ppx-instrumentation requirement.

findings.summary: ROUND-1 FINDING NOT CLOSED — never dispatched. Outcomes are still joined to catalogued sites by (basename, line) alone, consuming duplicates in list order and never refusing. Two mutants on one line have their KILLED/SURVIVED verdicts silently swapped, and a kill is written against the wrong site under attribution singleton_executed_set.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:1726 `let base p = Filename.basename p` with the predicate `sel.sel_site.s_line = m.line && base sel.sel_site.s_file = base m.file`. EXECUTED probe C (two mutants on lib/a/main.ml:15, cols 3-9 repl true and 11-15 repl false; engine reported m2=KILLED m1=SURVIVED): run exit 0, DB returned 3|9|true|m1|KILLED and 11|15|false|m2|SURVIVED — inverted. Probe B (same basename, different dirs): kill row lib/a/main.ml|t_alpha|singleton_executed_set and JSON certification self_certifying. findings.fix: Port the nine checks to node so the gate can execute them, keeping the same exit convention (0 passes, 1 assertion fired, >=2 error) and the same red-verification; or keep them in bash and wire them into CI as a step that distinguishes exit 1 from >=2, and stop linking them as gate checks. findings.summary: THE JOIN IS DECIDED BY THE LEXICAL FORM OF THE CATALOGUE'S IDENTIFIERS. load_generic writes a SYNTHESISED id — the report's physical line counter — into the same `id : string` field that carries a real engine id, and join arm 1 cross-checks only line and path. A catalogue numbered 1,2 is misjoined in report order and silently commits inverted verdicts; the IDENTICAL report against a catalogue named m1,m2 refuses. No fixture using named ids can ever see this, and every reasonable fixture uses named ids — which is why two rewrites shrank the defect without removing it: both corrected the symptom, and the symptom is the only thing visible from inside a well-named fixture.
findings.evidence: arch_mutants.ml:450 `id = Option.value ~default:(string_of_int !n) (str "id")` where !n is the report file's physical line counter; load_mutaml does the same at :520. EXECUTED with catalogue ids 1/2 and a report carrying no id: exit 0, DB holds cols 3-9 = KILLED and cols 11-15 = SURVIVED — inverted — completed=1, one kill row. CONTROL, byte-identical report, ids renamed m1/m2: exit 1, refusing as INDISTINGUISHABLE. The refusal message prints the synthetic ordinal as 'engine id "1"', surfacing the field confusion in its own diagnostic. checks/outcome-join-is-site-identity.js cannot see it: all four probes give every entry an explicit id.

findings.summary: THE ROUND'S OWN FIX REOPENED THE DEFECT IT CLOSED, THROUGH ITS ERROR PATH. tracked_by tests `Sys.command ... = 0`, so EVERY non-zero exit reads as 'not tracked' -- conflating 'no' with 'I could not tell'. The repository then refuses its own artefact claiming it belongs to another tree: finding :1133 verbatim, by a new route.
findings.evidence: FOUND BY THE FALSIFICATION READ AND REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY BY THE REVIEWER. Measured in a scratch repo: with a readable index `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- f.txt` exits 0; after `chmod 000 .git/index` it exits 128 while `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` still exits 0 -- rev-parse does not read the index. So the Some g/Some m branch IS reached, tracked_by answers false for a TRACKED file, the marker shrinks the boundary, and the diagnosis asserts either that there is no git repository or that the repository does not track the marker. Both false. The falsifier's own run, on the same fixture as probe 2 with the marker committed, printed exit 1 and foreign-tree claim=true, the ONLY difference from its passing control being chmod 000 on the index. Neither tree-boundary check has a probe where git fails other than by 'untracked'.
findings.fix: Distinguish the three answers git can give: tracked (0), untracked (1), and COULD NOT DETERMINE (anything else, 128 among them). The third must not silently become 'untracked' -- the conservative direction here is to keep the enclosing repository's boundary, or to refuse with a diagnosis that says the index could not be read. Add a probe where ls-files fails for a reason other than untracked; its absence is why the fix shipped.

summary:
ROUND 5 NO-GO, AND THE NO-GO IS NARROW: one HIGH remains open, and it was produced BY this round. Everything the round set out to do, it did, and the reviewer verified each closure by content and re-proved every ratchet red rather than accepting the agent that wrote it.

WHAT CLOSED. The five assertions that did not weigh what their labels announced. One of them was not weak but INVERTED -- red where the property held, green where it was violated -- and was DELETED rather than strengthened, seven assertions instead of eight, one green fewer deliberately; an inverted probe is green on the old code, so no red-on-old-tree check would ever have caught it, which is the probe-liveness sweep earning its place. The ownership gate, which answered 'is this finding MENTIONED anywhere' while claiming to answer 'does it have an owner'. And the HIGH from round 4: tracked_by conflating 'no' with 'I could not tell'.

THE TEST THAT SEPARATES A VALUE THAT EXISTS FROM ONE THAT ACTS. A third answer helps only if a caller does something different with it. Collapsing Undetermined's ACTION onto Untracked's -- same diagnosis, build exit 0, binary mtime CONFIRMED moved -- turns the check red with six assertions. The reviewer's first two attempts at this were INVALID and are recorded: one did not compile and the binary never moved, so the check measured the previous build and returned green; and the reviewer's own `dune build | tail; echo $?` read TAIL's exit code, printing build=0 over a failed build. A control that does not rebuild is not a control, and a pipeline's status is its LAST element's.

WHAT THE FALSIFICATION READ FOUND, and it is why this is NO-GO. R5-A's repair removed a typographic false-red and OPENED A COVERAGE HOLE on the defect its own finding names: the replacement vocabulary knows two phrasings and not the original one, so a fallback path asserting the nesting passes green. Reproduced by the reviewer with ONE thing changed -- the first attempt changed two and would have 'refuted' a correct report.

AND THE GATE'S REPAIR EXPOSED THAT OWNERSHIP HAD BEEN FICTIONAL. Fifteen of twenty-one ownerships rested on a path substring and a bare line number found SEPARATELY anywhere in a section; one finding was claimed by nine sections; a paragraph using three line numbers as OUTPUT SIZES claimed three findings; and a section stating that a finding was never looked at, followed by its fingerprint, CLOSED it. Documenting a finding closed it, and the more thorough the document the more it closed. The published figures are marked UNRECOVERABLE -- not wrong, since it was never shown the nineteen were unowned, and not left standing either.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED AND IS NAMED RATHER THAN LEFT: ownership now proves a commit touching the path plus a tracked check, and does NOT prove the commit's work is RELATED to the finding. Three discriminators were built and correctly killed. The remedy is SAMPLING -- revert-and-re-run over a random sample with N and the selection stated -- which is unaffordable per finding and affordable per round, and it enters the next round's plan ranked with everything else rather than promoted for being the freshest known gap.

THE STREAK PERSISTS AND ITS COMPOSITION CHANGED, which is the reading the split makes possible and the round-4 verdict could not. novel-finding-streak fires again -- two consecutive strike rounds ending at round 5 -- and it is recorded, not silenced. But round 4's streak was 7 of 13 findings about its own output, and round 5's is 1 of 4. The review is still finding new defects; it is far less often finding defects IT JUST CREATED. A streak counts findings; the split says where they come from, and only the second answers whether the fix rate was the problem.

THE DENOMINATOR: recomputed per CLOSURE rather than per finding produced -- because the first conflates how much was fixed with how much was broken -- round 4 is 0.50 self-produced defects per closure and round 5 is 0.14. A SPECIES CLAIM MADE HERE WAS RETRACTED: 'round 5's closures are all fixed-with-ratchet where round 4's were mostly subject-absent' was an artefact of the field being COMPUTED on one side and HAND-WRITTEN on the other. Recomputed identically, both rounds are subject-absent+ratcheted -- 7 of 7 and 12 of 14. Comparing two fields produced by different methods is not a comparison. Also corrected here: round 4 produced FOURTEEN findings, not the thirteen this verdict first published.

AND THE SURVIVING CLAIM WAS AUDITED THE SAME WAY, since it was the only one left. Its numerator was hand-classified on both sides -- symmetrical, so bias rather than method mismatch. Recomputed mechanically from the files each round's commits touched: 0.79 per closure to 0.29, against 0.50 to 0.14 by hand. The direction survives a differently-produced numerator, and the hand reading undercounts on BOTH sides rather than flattering the recent one. Neither numerator is the truth -- the mechanical one over-counts, the hand one is a judgement -- and what is established is that the comparison does not depend on which is used.
replay_provenance_note: Every OPEN finding now carries `last_replayed_at`. A finding is a statement ABOUT A COMMIT; OPEN is a value someone set at a past commit, not a measurement against HEAD. Of 25 open, 21 were seen by a specialist reading 618acb9 during round 3; 4 were INHERITED from rounds 1-2 and had never been replayed. Replaying those 4 found ALL 4 describing code that is no longer there -- including one of the three CRITICALs. The open-findings census is a count of claims about past trees.
merge_order_rule: REPLAY BEFORE YOU MERGE, AND THE ORDER IS NOT A PREFERENCE. Two inflations compose here -- duplicates keyed on a coordinate, and statuses never re-measured -- and collapsing them in the wrong order destroys evidence irreversibly. Replay first: :1726 is marked closed on its OWN evidence, and the surviving CRITICAL routes then dedupe into one live finding that keeps its own status. Dedupe first: :1726 merges into the live CRITICAL BEFORE anyone replays it, and the merged record inherits ONE status for two differently-aged claims -- and 'NOT CLOSED' is the label most likely to survive a merge, being the more alarming one. That launders a stale status into a live record and cannot be undone afterwards. When routes do merge, KEEP EACH ROUTE'S last_replayed_at rather than collapsing to one: the merged finding's age is the age of its OLDEST unreplayed route, not of its freshest.
census_shrank_defect_did_not: READ THE CORRECTED CENSUS AS BOOKKEEPING, NOT AS PROGRESS. Four stale findings does NOT mean the defect is smaller. The round-3 architect diagnosed the CRITICAL at DESIGN level against 618acb9 -- that finding is live and recently measured. :1726 describing a symptom that is now closed is fully compatible with the underlying defect being entirely live by another route, and it is: load_generic still writes a synthesised ordinal into the field carrying a real engine id, and join arm 1 still trusts it. The count went down. The defect did not. Anyone reading the smaller number as movement on the thing rather than on the ledger has read it backwards.
dedupe_note:
REPLAY RAN FIRST, THEN THIS. The order is not a preference: merging first would have made one record inherit ONE status for differently-aged claims, and 'ROUND-1 FINDING NOT CLOSED' -- the more alarming label -- is the one that survives a merge. :1726 was marked closed on ITS OWN evidence before any merge. Each route keeps its own prior_last_replayed_at: a merged finding's age is that of its OLDEST unreplayed route, not its freshest.
TWO DEFECTS WERE COUNTED AS FIVE ROWS. Routes {450,451} are one defect (a synthesised ordinal reaching the first join arm, found by a reviewer and an architect independently); routes {1393,1726} are one defect (the basename join). The normalizer fingerprints on path:line:category, and a coordinate does not identify an object across a rebase. That inflated the CRITICAL count from 1 to 3 -- a severity census that DRIVES TRIAGE, not a tidiness problem.

independence_note: THE GO WAS DRAFTED AND NOT PERSISTED. The convergence gate reported a procedural absence; what the absence covered was a missing contradictor. Filling the fields would have produced a compliant record of an uncontradicted GO -- and this is an item whose every previous round found a defect the round before believed closed. status_note: THE DRAFTED GO WAS FALSIFIED. It was never rendered, and this is why: an independent read broke four of its eight claims, one of them with a live HIGH.
streak_discriminator: THE STREAK HAS AN ANSWER, AND IT IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE ONE. Splitting the 13 findings this round produced by whether they concern code ROUND 4 ITSELF WROTE: 7 are about round-4 output, 6 are about surface that already existed. Findings about pre-existing code mean the review WIDENED its focus, and that terminates -- each new technique has a one-time yield, and the probe-liveness sweep and the falsification mandate were both first-use tonight. Findings about code this round created are NEW SURFACE, and that is the category that decides convergence. At 7 of 13, the process is generating defects at roughly the rate it closes them -- including a HIGH that IS its own fix. So the streak is not merely a widening lens: THE FIX RATE IS THE PROBLEM, NOT THE FINDING RATE, and no number of further rounds converges on its own. Round 5's plan must change how fixes are made, not how findings are hunted.
closure_species_note:
CLOSURES ARE RECORDED BY SPECIES, because the species have different failure modes and stating them as one lets a subject-absent closure inherit a ratcheted one's confidence. subject-absent: the subject is gone, NOTHING guards its return, and it reopens SILENTLY -- which is exactly what this round's HIGH did, :1133 returning through the error path of its own fix. fixed-with-ratchet: a guard exists and the guard can itself be checked for liveness. The two are not exclusive and the strongest closure is BOTH. This round: {'subject-absent+ratcheted': 12, 'fixed-with-ratchet': 1, 'subject-absent-only': 1}.
A CORRECTION TO THIS VERY FIELD, recorded rather than quietly amended: the first classifier tested for SUBJECT-ABSENT before testing for a ratchet, so it reported 13 subject-absent and 1 ratcheted -- an either/or over a question whose answer is a pair. An instrument narrower than its question, in the tool built to audit that class, on the same night it was named four times.
round5_acceptance_criterion:
ROUND 5 CHANGES THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, NOT THE FINDING PROCESS -- which is what 7-of-13 says is needed. THE RULE: every fix must carry a probe ON ITS OWN ERROR PATH, and it must answer, BY EXECUTION rather than by argument: what does this do when the thing it calls FAILS? For every Sys.command, every external invocation, every parse, every database read -- does the fix distinguish a FAILURE from a NEGATIVE ANSWER, and is there a probe that exercises the failure? THE SEVERITIES POINT THE SAME WAY, AGAINST THE INTUITION THAT SEVERITY ORDERS THE WORK. The HIGH fails LOUDLY: a tracked file read as untracked makes the repository REFUSE its own artefact -- visible, blocking, self-announcing. A vacuous probe fails SILENTLY, and what it lets through is THE NEXT FIX. The HIGH's fix is then the FIRST work the repaired criterion is applied to, which doubles as a test of the criterion: if that fix passes a criterion enforced by non-vacuous probes and STILL reopens something, the criterion is wrong and we learn it on the first use rather than the seventh.

round5_ordering_after_falsification:
ORDER: falsifier reports -> if it holds the seven claims AND answers the matcher question -> FIX THE OWNERSHIP GATE -> then the HIGH, as the criterion's first readable test.

THE GATE COMES FIRST FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN THE ONE THAT PUT PROBES BEFORE THE HIGH, and the difference is worth stating because conflating them would generalise a bad rule. That earlier argument was DEPENDENCY: the acceptance criterion was unenforceable while a probe could be vacuous. This is not that shape. A broken ownership gate CANNOT make a correct fix incorrect; it only makes an unhandled finding look handled. It does not touch the HIGH's correctness at all.

IT TOUCHES WHETHER THE RESULT CAN BE READ. The HIGH's fix is the first application of the repaired criterion and therefore its TEST -- and A TEST WHOSE OUTCOME IS RECORDED BY A BROKEN RECORDER IS NOT A TEST YOU CAN READ. If the fix lands and the gate says 'handled', nobody can tell whether it says so because the work was done or because an outcome section mentioned a fingerprint. That would spend the round's most informative moment on an unreadable measurement.

THE RISK IS RECURRING, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. R5-A tripped this gate WHILE WRITING ABOUT WHY IT WOULD STAY RED. The HIGH's group will write a brief and an outcome section in the same register about the same findings. The only mitigation available today is 'remember not to write bare fingerprints' -- MANUAL DISCIPLINE, which has already failed once tonight for this team, on the one-writer rule, in a session where the orchestrator was personally enforcing it. AND THE GATE IS EXACTING A LIVE COST RIGHT NOW: four findings are deliberately left unnamed in the brief, because naming them would CLOSE them. The gate is forcing work to be left undocumented in order to keep it honest. That state must not persist through another group.

DO NOT FIX THE GATE BEFORE THE FALSIFIER REPORTS. Its mandate includes establishing BY EXECUTION whether the matcher can distinguish a group that HANDLED a finding from a document that MENTIONS one, and that answer determines what the fix is. Fixing first would repair a mechanism whose defect is characterised but not measured -- the shape refused when a cleverer pattern was declined for probe 4. ownership_fix_ceiling:
THE FIX'S CEILING, NAMED BEFORE IT IS BUILT, the same way R4-D's was. An explicit owner field is the right structure and it does NOT close the class -- it closes the ACCIDENTAL half. It removes ownership claimed by a paragraph that happened to contain a path and a digit. It CANNOT remove an agent that writes `owner: R5-B` for work it did not do: a field written deliberately can be written falsely, by an agent under pressure to show coverage.
So the scope is MAKE OWNERSHIP DELIBERATE, NOT TRUTHFUL. A group told to make ownership trustworthy will report success when it has made it explicit. What makes a deliberate claim checkable is the same thing that makes an assertion checkable -- something OUTSIDE the claim that can contradict it: a finding marked owned must name the commit and the check that closed it, and a claim with neither is a claim, not a closure.

ownership_relatedness_gap:
THE GAP R5-B COULD NOT CLOSE IS SAMPLABLE, and sampling is the standard answer to a check that is correct and too expensive -- which neither the reviewer nor the roadmap session reached for once tonight. The gap: nothing distinguishes 'the commit contains work RELATED to the finding' from 'the commit touches the same file'. R5-B killed three discriminators correctly -- line proximity dies on findings at line 0 or 1, of which this verdict has several; a fingerprint in the commit message is self-corroborating, the same agent writing both in one breath; revert-plus-re-run is the right question and too expensive PER FINDING.
But it is unaffordable only EXHAUSTIVELY. Revert-and-re-run over a RANDOM SAMPLE OF N ownership records, with N and the selection method stated, converts an impossible check into an estimate -- and an estimate with a declared sample is enormously better than the current position, which is that nothing distinguishes the two at all. Five of five surviving is real evidence; one of five failing is a live defect no exhaustive check would ever have been run to find. THE RATCHET CANNOT AFFORD IT, BUT A ROUND CAN.
round5_split:
THE NUMBER THE ROUND EXISTS TO PRODUCE: 1 of 4 findings this round produced concern code ROUND 5 ITSELF WROTE; 3 concern pre-existing surface. Round 4 was SEVEN of THIRTEEN. The acceptance criterion -- every fix carries a probe on its own error path, answered by execution -- was round 5's whole intervention, and this is the ratio it was meant to move. IT MOVED, from 54% to 25%. READ IT WITH ITS CAVEATS, both of which cut against the flattering reading: the denominators differ (13 against 4), so this is a direction and not a rate; and the one round-5-output finding is a HIGH -- a repair that opened a coverage hole on the very defect its own finding named -- so the class did not disappear, it got rarer and stayed severe.

THE DENOMINATOR WAS WRONG ON BOTH SIDES, AND CORRECTING IT STRENGTHENS THE RESULT. 'Findings produced this round' conflates HOW MUCH WAS FIXED with HOW MUCH WAS BROKEN: a round that ships fewer or smaller fixes produces fewer self-inflicted defects with no improvement in method at all, and the ratio falls because the denominator falls with it. The criterion was introduced to answer DOES A FIX NOW BREAK LESS OFTEN, so the denominator must name the WORK.
Recomputed per CLOSURE: round 4 is 7 self-produced findings against 14 closures = 0.50; round 5 is 1 against 7 = 0.14. That is a stronger statement than 1-of-4 AND it measures the thing that was intervened on. With n this small it is a direction, not a rate, on either denominator.

AND A CORRECTION TO A FIGURE THIS VERDICT ALREADY PUBLISHED: round 4 produced FOURTEEN findings, not thirteen. '7 of 13' was taken before the set was complete -- a count true at the moment it was read and stale by the time it was quoted, which is the defect this task has spent two rounds naming. The split is 7 of 14, and the direction is unchanged.

A QUALITATIVE DIFFERENCE THE RATIO HIDES, and it is the strongest evidence here. Round 4's closures were 12 subject-absent-plus-ratcheted, 1 ratcheted only, 1 subject-absent only: mostly findings whose SUBJECT HAD GONE AWAY. Round 5's seven are ALL fixed-with-ratchet -- every one closed by a fix carrying a proven-red guard, none by the subject having vanished. So round 5 did more actual FIXING per closure and produced fewer defects doing it. Two independent movements in the same direction, which a single ratio would have reported as one.
species_claim_retracted:
RETRACTED IN FULL: 'round 5's closures are ALL fixed-with-ratchet where round 4's were mostly subject-absent' was called the strongest evidence in this verdict, and it was an ARTEFACT OF HOW THE FIELD WAS PRODUCED. Round 4's species were COMPUTED by a classifier; round 5's were HAND-WRITTEN by the reviewer during the closure pass, hardcoded to fixed-with-ratchet. Recomputed with the SAME classifier on both sides: round 4 is 12 subject-absent+ratcheted, 1 ratcheted only, 1 subject-absent only; ROUND 5 IS 7 SUBJECT-ABSENT+RATCHETED OUT OF 7. Both rounds closed findings in the same way. There is no qualitative difference, and the 'two independent movements in the same direction' claim had ONE movement in it.

THE GENERAL FORM, and it is worse than the compositional confound that prompted the check: COMPARING TWO FIELDS PRODUCED BY DIFFERENT METHODS IS NOT A COMPARISON. One side computed, one side written by hand, same name, same file, same schema -- and nothing in the record said so. The field carried no statement of its own provenance, which is the identical defect this verdict documents elsewhere as a reading that does not say which convention produced it. Every closure record now carries closure_species_method.

WHAT SURVIVES: the per-closure ratio, 0.50 against 0.14, which is computed the same way on both sides from data neither round hand-wrote. It is a direction and not a rate at this n, and it is now the ONLY evidence that the criterion moved anything. The compositional confound raised against the species claim never had to be answered -- the claim did not survive its own audit.
surviving_claim_audited:
THE AUDIT THAT KILLED THE SPECIES CLAIM WAS RUN ON THE ONE THAT SURVIVED IT, and the surviving claim came out STRONGER. Its denominator was already recomputed with one classifier over both rounds. Its NUMERATOR -- 'findings concerning code the round itself wrote' -- had not been audited, and it was HAND-CLASSIFIED on both sides by the reviewer: round 4's when the discriminator was first proposed, round 5's DURING ROUND 5'S OWN CLOSING PASS, which is exactly the position that produced the species artefact.

FIRST RESULT: the method was SYMMETRICAL. Both sides hand-classified by the same person under the same reading, so the risk was bias, not the method mismatch that destroyed the species claim.

SECOND RESULT, and it is the one that matters: recomputed MECHANICALLY -- a finding counts as own-output when its path is among the files that round's commits touched, derived from git and identically on both sides -- round 4 is 11 of 14 produced, 0.79 per closure; round 5 is 2 of 4, 0.29 per closure. THE DIRECTION SURVIVES A DIFFERENTLY-PRODUCED NUMERATOR: 0.79 to 0.29 computed, 0.50 to 0.14 by hand. Two numerators built by different methods, each symmetric across the rounds, both falling by a factor near three.

AND THE BIAS CHECK COMES OUT CLEAN, which is not what was expected: the hand classification UNDERCOUNTS against the mechanical proxy on BOTH sides -- 7 against 11, and 1 against 2 -- roughly proportionally. It did not flatter the recent side. The four round-4 disagreements and the one in round 5 are recorded rather than reconciled.

NEITHER NUMERATOR IS THE TRUTH, and saying so is part of the result. The mechanical proxy OVER-counts: a finding on a pre-existing part of a file the round happened to touch is counted as own-output. The hand reading asked the narrower question -- does this concern code the round WROTE -- and is a judgement. They measure different things. What is established is that the comparison does not depend on which one is used, which is more than either could establish alone.
